config.title: Design Notification System

intro.title: Design Notification System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification system that displays messages to users, such as alerts or updates, within an Angular application. You will learn how to use Angular services to manage and share notification data across different components. The core programming concept involves creating a service to handle the state of notifications and using component templates to display them. You will work with TypeScript classes, Angular's dependency injection, and basic HTML structure to implement this feature.
intro.usecase: Notification systems are essential in modern web applications where users need timely feedback about system events. In e-commerce platforms like Amazon, notifications alert users about order confirmations, shipping updates, and price drops. Social media apps like Facebook use notifications to show new messages, friend requests, and activity alerts. Dashboard applications display real-time notifications for system alerts, data updates, or user messages, keeping users informed without disrupting their workflow.

objectives: Construct a notification service using Angular's dependency injection system
Initialize and manage notification state with reactive data structures
Implement notification components with configurable types and templates
Bind notification data to component templates using Angular's data binding syntax
Configure notification display duration and auto-dismiss behavior
Integrate the notification service across multiple application components
Manipulate notification queues for proper display ordering and lifecycle management
Render dynamic notification content based on user interactions and application events

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and Notification interface
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and create a Notification interface with id, message, type, and timestamp properties.
steps.hint: Use the import statement for Component and define an interface with the specified properties and appropriate TypeScript types.

seedCode.App.tsx: // Import Component from '@angular/core' and create Notification interface here

steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the Component import and a Notification interface ready for use in the notification system.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and a Notification interface with id (string), message (string), type (string), and timestamp (Date) properties is defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported Component from '@angular/core' and defined all four properties (id, message, type, timestamp) in the Notification interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't meet the requirements. You need to import Component from '@angular/core' and create a Notification interface with id, message, type, and timestamp properties.

steps.title: Create the NotificationComponent class
steps.instruction: Create the NotificationComponent class with the @Component decorator. Define the selector as 'app-notification' and set the templateUrl to './notification.component.html'.
steps.hint: Use the Component decorator from '@angular/core' that you imported earlier. The class should be named NotificationComponent and export it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationComponent class is defined with proper Angular component metadata.
successCriteria: NotificationComponent class exists with @Component decorator, selector 'app-notification', and templateUrl './notification.component.html'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have the @Component decorator with selector 'app-notification' and templateUrl './notification.component.html'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't complete. Check that you have the @Component decorator with the correct selector and templateUrl.

steps.title: Initialize notifications array in component state
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationComponent class, add a property named 'notifications' with the type 'Notification[]' and initialize it as an empty array.
steps.hint: Define the property directly in the class body, using TypeScript type annotation for the array of Notification objects.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a notifications property that can store notification data.
successCriteria: The NotificationComponent class contains a 'notifications' property typed as Notification[] and initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check the type annotation or initialization. It should be 'notifications: Notification[] = []'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications property is missing or incorrectly defined. Add 'notifications: Notification[] = []' inside the class.

steps.title: Create addNotification handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationComponent class, create a method named addNotification that takes two parameters: message (string) and type (either 'success', 'error', or 'info'). This method should create a new notification object with a unique id (you can use Date.now() for simplicity), and add it to the notifications array.
steps.hint: Remember to use the Notification interface for the new object. You can generate a unique id with Date.now().
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can programmatically add new notifications to the state.
successCriteria: The addNotification method is defined with correct parameters, creates a notification object with id, message, and type, and pushes it to the notifications array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the method, but make sure it creates a complete notification object with id, message, and type, and adds it to the notifications array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addNotification method is missing or incorrect. It should take message and type parameters, create a notification object, and push it to the notifications array.

steps.title: Create removeNotification handler method
steps.instruction: In the NotificationComponent class, create a method named removeNotification that takes an id parameter of type number and filters out the notification with that id from the notifications array.
steps.hint: Use the filter method on the notifications array to keep only notifications whose id does not match the provided id.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a removeNotification method that can remove notifications by their id.
successCriteria: The removeNotification method is defined, takes an id parameter of type number, and correctly filters the notifications array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the removeNotification method, but make sure it correctly filters the notifications array to remove the notification with the matching id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeNotification method is missing or incorrect. It should take an id parameter and update the notifications array by filtering out the matching notification.

steps.title: Set up the component template structure
steps.instruction: In the component decorator, create the template with a main container div and a section for displaying notifications. Add a <div> with class 'notification-container' and inside it add a <section> with class 'notification-list'.
steps.hint: Update the template property in the @Component decorator to include the HTML structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic HTML structure ready to display notifications.
successCriteria: The template property contains a div with class 'notification-container' and a nested section with class 'notification-list'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the container div and the notification-list section.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is incomplete. Check that you have a div with class 'notification-container' and a section with class 'notification-list' inside it.

steps.title: Display notifications using *ngFor
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a <div> element that uses *ngFor to iterate through the notifications array and display each notification's message and type.
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngFor structural directive to loop through the notifications array. Display the message and type properties of each notification object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Using *ngFor to display list items
  • {{ item.name }} - {{ item.category }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template should contain a <div> with *ngFor directive that displays notification.message and notification.type for each item in the notifications array.
successCriteria: The template includes a <div> element with *ngFor="let notification of notifications" that displays {{ notification.message }} and {{ notification.type }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your *ngFor directive correctly references the notifications array and displays both message and type properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet include the *ngFor directive to display notifications. Remember to use *ngFor="let notification of notifications" and show both message and type.

steps.title: Add notification type styling classes
steps.instruction: In the notification item template, add an [ngClass] binding to apply CSS classes based on the notification's type property. Use classes like 'info', 'success', 'warning', and 'error'.
steps.hint: Use [ngClass] with an object expression that maps notification.type values to CSS class names.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: applying conditional CSS classes
Content
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification div will have conditional CSS classes applied based on its type property.
successCriteria: The notification item template uses [ngClass] with an object expression that maps notification.type values to appropriate CSS class names.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your [ngClass] binding correctly maps notification.type values to CSS class names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notification items don't have the required [ngClass] binding for conditional styling.

steps.title: Add close button to each notification
steps.instruction: Add a close button inside each notification's <div> element in the template. The button should have the text 'Close' and use Angular event binding to call the removeNotification method with the notification's id when clicked.
steps.hint: Place a <button> element inside the inner <div> that displays the notification message. Use (click)="removeNotification(notification.id)" to bind the click event.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click binding
<button (click)="handleClick(item.id)">Remove</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification will have a 'Close' button that, when clicked, removes that specific notification from the list.
successCriteria: A <button> element with text 'Close' is added inside each notification's inner <div>, and its (click) event is bound to removeNotification(notification.id).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it's inside the inner <div> and uses the correct event binding: (click)="removeNotification(notification.id)".
steps.feedbackWrong: The close button is missing or not properly configured. Add a <button> with 'Close' text and bind its click event to call removeNotification with the notification's id.

steps.title: Add notification controls and test buttons
steps.instruction: Add a button for each notification type (info, success, error) that calls the addNotification method with appropriate parameters when clicked. Place these buttons above the notifications list in the template.
steps.hint: Create three buttons with click handlers that call addNotification with different message strings and type values. Use the existing addNotification method signature.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding test buttons in template
<button (click)="addNotification('Info message', 'info')">Info</button>
<button (click)="addNotification('Success message', 'success')">Success</button>
<button (click)="addNotification('Error message', 'error')">Error</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Three buttons appear above the notifications list that add notifications of different types when clicked.
successCriteria: Three buttons with click handlers calling addNotification with appropriate message and type parameters are added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some buttons, but make sure you have all three types (info, success, error) with proper click handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test buttons aren't properly implemented. Check that you have three buttons with (click) handlers calling addNotification.
